title: Responses to Microbial Challenges by SLAMF Receptors
authors: Boaz Job van Driel; Gongxian Liao; Pablo Engel; Cox Terhorst
id: Matched: SLAMF Receptors Alter Cytokine Production by Phagocytes
abstract: This review examines how SLAMF receptors sense and respond to microbial challenges. These receptors modulate immune cell functions, influencing microbicidal activity and phagocyte migration.

title: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced Macrophage Activation and Signal Transduction in the Absence of Src-Family Kinases Hck, Fgr, and Lyn
authors: Fanying Meng; Clifford A. Lowell
abstract: This study investigated LPS-induced macrophage activation in mice lacking Src-family kinases Hck, Fgr, and Lyn. Macrophages from these mice showed no major defects in LPS-induced activation, indicating these kinases are not obligatory for LPS signaling.

authors: Ninghai Wang; Abhay Satoskar; William Faubion; Duncan Howie; Susumu Okamoto; Stefan Feske; Charles G...
id: Matched: Impaired Responses to LPS by SLAM−/− Macrophages.
abstract: SLAM controls T cell IL-4 secretion and macrophage cytokine production. SLAM deficiency impairs parasite clearance, highlighting its role in innate and acquired immunity.

title: SLAM Family Receptors Regulate Immunity with and without SAP-related Adaptors
authors: André Veillette

abstract: This study investigated the immune phenotypes of mice lacking SLAM and 2B4 receptors. The findings demonstrate the critical role of these SLAM family receptors in regulating T cell, macrophage, and NK cell functions.

title: SLAMF1 is required for TLR4-mediated TRAM-TRIF–dependent signaling in human macrophages
authors: Maria Yurchenko; Astrid Skjesol; Liv Ryan; Gabriel Mary Richard; Richard Kumaran Kandasamy; Ninghai ...
abstract: SLAMF1's role in TLR4-mediated, MyD88-independent signaling in human macrophages was investigated. SLAMF1 enhances type I interferon production induced by Gram-negative bacteria.

authors: Katja Sæterhaug Bye; Kristin Rian; Liv Ryan; Terje Espevik; Marit W. Anthonsen; Maria Yurchenko

abstract: This study investigated how TLR4 and SLAMF1 receptors influence TNF release by human metapneumovirus in macrophages. The findings show these receptors regulate TNF and IFN-β release via p38 MAPK, suggesting a therapeutic target.

abstract: This study investigated SLAMF7 and TLR pathway interactions in monocytes and macrophages. SLAMF7 enhances TLR-induced pro-inflammatory cytokine production, but not phagocytosis.

authors: Kaja Elisabeth Nilsen; Boyao Zhang; Astrid Skjesol; Liv Ryan; Hilde Vagle; Maren Helene Bøe; Pontus ...
abstract: A peptide derived from SLAMF1 was studied for its anti-inflammatory properties. This peptide was found to prevent TLR4-mediated inflammation and mortality in vivo by blocking key signaling interactions.

title: SLAM Family Receptor Signaling in Viral Infections: HIV and Beyond
authors: Patrick O’Connell; Andrea Amalfitano; Yasser A. Aldhamen
abstract: This paper reviews SLAM family receptor signaling in immune cells and its role in viral infections, particularly HIV. These receptors, regulated by adaptor proteins, can be targeted by viruses, influencing immune responses.

title: Macrophage Polarization: Different Gene Signatures in M1(LPS+) vs. Classically and M2(LPS–) vs. Alternatively Activated Macrophages
authors: Marco Orecchioni, Yanal Ghosheh, Akula Bala Pramod, Klaus Ley
abstract: This study compared gene expression in *in vivo* M1/M2 macrophages with *in vitro* classically/alternatively activated macrophages. The findings indicate that *in vivo* M1/M2 polarization is not equivalent to *in vitro* activation states.

abstract: SLAMF1 receptor interaction with *Trypanosoma cruzi* was studied using six parasite strains. This interaction influences parasite load, NADPH oxidase expression, and ROS production in a strain-dependent manner, affecting host survival.

abstract: SLAMF7 was studied for its role in doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity and macrophage inflammation. SLAMF7 restrains pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, protecting against cardiac damage.

authors: Yongjian Wu; Qiaohua Wang; Miao Li; Juanfeng Lao; Huishu Tang; Siqi Ming; Minhao Wu; Sitang Gong; Li...
abstract: SLAMF7's expression increases in sepsis and it suppresses macrophage inflammatory signaling. SLAMF7 protects against lethal sepsis by reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines and organ damage.

abstract: Quantitative proteomics analyzed macrophage responses to *Trypanosoma cruzi* infection, revealing strain-dependent and SLAMF1-mediated immune regulation. Different parasite strains induce distinct macrophage responses, impacting infection control and host survival.
